clue.text: Man of words caught in entrance wearing long pants?

indicators.note: the word in tells us the abbreviation for caught sits inside the doorway word

parts.note: an entrance is a door
long johns are long underpants, so the pants give the johns part
wearing clothes is having them on

explanation.surface: A wordsmith stuck in a doorway in his long trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Samuel Johnson compiled the great 1755 Dictionary of the English Language, hence 'Man of words'. Long johns are thermal underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous lexicographer was the supreme eighteenth-century man of letters and dictionary maker.

clue.text: Comes from the German saint

parts.note: der is a German word for the
St Ives, a saint known by the name Ives

explanation.surface: Something originates with a German holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive is to originate or descend from a source, so it equals comes from.

clue.text: Cocoa and chocolate are one originally

definitions.text: Cocoa and chocolate are one originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A remark that cocoa and chocolate come from the same source.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the cacao bean is the single origin of both cocoa and chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao tree's seeds are the raw material from which both cocoa and chocolate are made.

clue.text: Devotee of Verdi etc: if with article, of Pergolesi?

indicators.note: if with says the answer plus an extra letter would make the Pergolesi phrase, so that letter is removed here

parts.note: Pergolesi wrote opera buffa, Italian comic opera
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An opera lover, who with a small addition becomes an eighteenth-century Italian comic genre.
explanation.walkthrough: Add the article A to the answer and you get opera buffa, the comic opera form of Pergolesi's La serva padrona.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is an enthusiast, so a fan of Verdi and his kind is an enthusiast of opera.

clue.text: See 1
Container of tea drunk by kangaroo on its way?

indicators.note: drunk by says the tea container is swallowed inside the young kangaroo word

parts.note: a joey is a young kangaroo
an urn holds tea

explanation.surface: A kangaroo swigging a tea urn as it travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey is a passage or route from one place to another, a way travelled.

clue.text: 1 4's pet pig swallowing first of drugs, ecstasy

indicators.note: swallowing puts the letter inside the pig word

parts.note: a hog is a pig

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of drugs

parts.note: E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson's pet pig gulping drugs and ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Hodge was Dr Johnson's cat, fed on oysters; 1 4 points to the linked answer at 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson kept a cat by that name, immortalised by Boswell and a statue in Gough Square.

clue.text: Disposed of round flat note like sisters of chalk cliffs

indicators.note: round says the sold word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: goods disposed of are sold
flat means level or even
F is a musical note

explanation.surface: Something sold around a flat note, compared to a famous coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: The Seven Sisters are chalk cliffs on the Sussex coast of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seven Sisters are a set of seven cliffs, so something like them comes in sevens.

clue.text: Devotee of nature creating hell among teachers

indicators.note: among puts the hell word inside the teachers' union abbreviation

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union
Dis is the classical underworld, hell

explanation.surface: A nature lover causing chaos in the staff room.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about unclothed, in the state of nature, so 'devotee of nature' fits.

clue.text: Dickensian number from Orange?

parts.note: Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations
a PIN is a personal identification number

explanation.surface: A character from Dickens comes from a place called Orange.
explanation.walkthrough: Orange suggests the fruit or the Dutch royal house, but it is Cox's Orange, the apple variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Cox's Orange Pippin is a popular English apple variety, so the apple name follows Orange.

clue.text: Cardinal supplied a lot of light gas in cereal for everyone

indicators.note: in places the gas fragment inside the cereal word

parts.note: rice is a cereal

indicators.note: a lot of keeps most of the gas name, dropping its last two letters

parts.note: helium is a very light gas
U is the film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A churchman receiving most of a light gas in his breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last two letters of the gas name. The U certificate in British cinema marks a film as fit for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Richelieu was the powerful French churchman and chief minister to Louis XIII.

clue.text: Harpist and painter as parent keeping 6

indicators.note: keeping says the parent word holds the number inside

parts.note: a dad is a parent
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A musician and artist who, as a father, looks after a child.
explanation.walkthrough: King David played the harp; Jacques-Louis David was a French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical king played the harp and the French neoclassical painter bore the same name.

clue.text: Shakespearean in the orchestra

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Twelfth Night who disguises herself as a boy
a stringed instrument a little larger than a violin

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a Twelfth Night heroine and to the alto member of the violin family.

clue.text: Write study of Ulster in Thackeray's history

parts.note: to pen is to write
a den is a study
NI is Northern Ireland, or Ulster, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a study of Northern Ireland, found in a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Ulster' stands for NI's, the possessive of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The History of Pendennis is the full title of Thackeray's 1848 to 1850 novel.

clue.text: Embittered note about Scots sweetheart to stay

indicators.note: about puts the sour word around the sweetheart

parts.note: embittered means sour
jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart, as in Burns

explanation.surface: A bitter remark about a Scottish lover being allowed to remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To sojourn is to stay somewhere temporarily.

clue.text: Use Jewish number 50 as coalition's new model?

definitions.text: Use Jewish number 50 as coalition's new model?

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Advice to the government to use a reshuffled set of letters as its template.
explanation.walkthrough: John Lewis is a British department store owned by its staff; the 2010 coalition praised its partnership model.
explanation.definitionFit: The employee-owned retailer's partnership was held up by the coalition government as a model for public services.

clue.text: Derisive comment on brute eating his head

indicators.note: eating puts the letter inside the brute word

parts.note: a Yahoo is a brutish human in Gulliver's Travels
his refers back to the brute, whose initial is B

explanation.surface: A jeer aimed at a beast devouring its own head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his head' is the first letter of 'brute' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is a schoolyard jeer of contempt, short for the longer taunting phrase with sucks.

clue.text: 1 4's 4 down, Jewish majority with one churchman

indicators.note: majority keeps most of the word, dropping its last two letters

parts.note: Hebrew can mean Jewish
I is the Roman numeral one
a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson's travels described by a Jewish majority with a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority' leaves HEBR. Johnson toured the Hebrides with Boswell in 1773 and wrote about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's 1773 trip to the Western Isles of Scotland was his tour of the Hebrides.

clue.text: Look at fellow during shuteye, say?

indicators.note: during puts the fellow letter inside the sleep word
say signals the eye sound is spelt as a single letter

parts.note: shuteye is sleep; its final sound matches the letter I

explanation.surface: Glancing at a man while he's asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Shufti is British slang, from Arabic, for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A shufti is British slang for a quick look or glance.

clue.text: Old copper leaves epic: coppers need muscle

indicators.note: leaves says the old penny letter departs from the epic

parts.note: the Iliad is Homer's epic
D was the old penny, a copper coin
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, so CUs are coppers

explanation.surface: A policeman abandons a long poem while other police need brawn.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for the pre-1971 British penny, a copper coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The iliacus is a muscle of the pelvis that flexes the hip.

clue.text: Polish part of Hungarian city backed with sound of drum

parts.note: to polish is to rub

indicators.note: backed means the city part is read in reverse

parts.note: Buda is one half of Budapest

explanation.surface: Polishing a part of Budapest to the beat of a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Rub-a-dub imitates the rolling beat of a drum.

clue.text: Borders capturing man in place of jackdaw

indicators.note: capturing says the borders word holds the man word

parts.note: rims are borders or edges
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: Frontiers trapping a man where a famous bird lived.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jackdaw of Rheims is a comic poem in the Ingoldsby Legends about a bird that steals a cardinal's ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ingoldsby Legends tell of the thieving jackdaw in the French cathedral city.

clue.text: 1 4's presenter to cry up source

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the cry word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: Dr Johnson's champion wanting to weep for a spring.
explanation.walkthrough: James Boswell wrote the Life of Samuel Johnson, presenting him to the world.
explanation.definitionFit: His biographer brought Johnson before the public in his celebrated Life.

clue.text: Month's shortly up: cover with extraordinary protection

indicators.note: cover with says the extraordinary word wraps around the month part

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means extraordinary

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the shortened month backwards
shortly cuts the last letter off the month

parts.note: July is a month

explanation.surface: Time running out, so wrap up with some special protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the month's final letter and 'up', in a down clue, turns what is left upwards before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccination given against influenza protects the recipient through winter.

clue.text: Old musical student at start of play in Liverpool street

indicators.note: in places the student and opening pieces inside the street name

parts.note: Lime Street is a main street and railway station in Liverpool
L is a learner driver, or student
Act I is the first act of a play

explanation.surface: A learner at the opening of a show staged on a street in Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac Time was a 1922 London operetta adapted from Schubert's music.

clue.text: 4 across playing Alice?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the name are acted about, rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor surnamed like the lexicographer taking the role of Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: Celia Johnson starred in Brief Encounter; '4 across' refers to the linked answer's second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The English actress of Brief Encounter fame shares the surname of the lexicographer.

clue.text: No way in which Jeremy has chains

definitions.meaning: a sailing boat head to wind with no steerage way is in this state
the English actor Jeremy of that surname

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers shackles, the actor's surname and the nautical state of being stalled head to wind.

clue.text: Narcotic work I take with hesitation

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A drug that a hesitant person takes with work.
explanation.definitionFit: The drug from poppies is a classic narcotic.

clue.text: The best thing is to get religious fellow elevated

parts.note: a Jew is a man of the Jewish religion
el is the elevated railway

explanation.surface: The ideal outcome is for a devout man to be promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: El is short for an elevated railway, as in Chicago.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewel is a prized thing, the gem or best of its kind.

clue.text: King of Wales, abandoning rugby, on direct path that's pointless

indicators.note: abandoning means the rugby letters are dropped from the Welsh name

parts.note: Cymru is the Welsh name for Wales
RU is Rugby Union

indicators.note: pointless says a compass point letter is removed

parts.note: a beeline is a direct path
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A Welsh monarch gives up rugby and goes straight for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' leaves CYM; 'pointless' takes an E from BEELINE to give BELINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbeline is the ancient British king of Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Prize for sexagenarian finding spring in a kiss

indicators.note: in puts the spring inside the kiss word

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A sixty-year-old's reward is a kiss full of youth.
explanation.walkthrough: In England a free bus pass is given at pension age, once 60.
explanation.definitionFit: The free travel card for older people is a treasured perk of reaching that age.

clue.text: Brute when the sheet's turned back?

indicators.note: turned back says the sheet word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lamina is a thin sheet or layer

explanation.surface: A beast, revealed when the bedcovers are pulled back.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is a beast or brute.
